title: PTP: Added support for Drift_Tracking TLV (802.1ASdm)

notes.body:
Can you please edit the commit message to start with "PTP: " or similar?

https://wiki.wireshark.org/Development/SubmittingPatches#writing-a-good-commit-message
Should this be `BASE_OUI`?
In the follow_up TLV it is also BASE_DEC

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18379/diffs?diff_id=1206157838&start_sha=757a81f019bcbb10f8eb617cde275b30046f96c5#c44b9cae397bb1b76ce465b29a7f38d6c27973f7_6529_6529)

According to IEEE guidelines, "The OUI is a 24-bit (three octet) sequence" (https://standards.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/import/documents/tutorials/eui.pdf)
and according to AS2020, the OrganizationId is an octet3. This concludes that it was wrong for PTP_Follow_up, Drift_Tracking TLV and for Signaling msg.

![image](/uploads/6eaecdcc048196ab58adf1960f1378f8/image.png){width=379 height=81}
BASE_OUI does not work, it must be BASE_DEC

A strings value isn't needed with `BASE_OUI` because it will automatically do the lookup in the OUI database. { 0x00, 0x80, 0xC2 } is registered to the IEEE 802.1 Chair ( "IEEE8021Chai", "IEEE 802.1 Chair") so if `BASE_OUI` is used that will be the result.

I realize that PTP is unusual because its uses the 802.1 assigned OUI in several places and the spec might insist that that OUI the only valid one. If you don't want to change it, I suppose that's reasonable.
Should this be a `FT_EUI64`? Note that will do manufacturer lookups if hardware address resolution is enabled.
Yes it seems you are right, I was trying to do it the same way (as done in different places). I will change it for my newlie added code.

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18379/diffs?diff_id=1206157838&start_sha=757a81f019bcbb10f8eb617cde275b30046f96c5#c44b9cae397bb1b76ce465b29a7f38d6c27973f7_6554_6554)

I changed it to FT_EUI64 for the `hf_ptp_as_dt_tlv_sync_grandmaster_identity'. If you like, I can fix the rest of the wrong `FT_UINT64` in the packet-ptp-c file. I would probably do this in a second commit.

![image](/uploads/a83e6dc47877c7e54b6f83c885455be7/image.png){width=377 height=102}
FT_EUI64 and BASE_HEX are not compatible. It must be BASE_NONE then it works.
Yes, that's right, thanks.
copy/pasted filter name (from item before) ?
Yes, displaying only `fractionalNanoseconds` is not practical as they are fractional.

I don't understand your comment. As it is, you are adding only `fractionalNanoseconds` to the tree:

`proto_tree_add_item(ptp_tlv_tree, hf_ptp_as_dt_tlv_sync_egress_timestamp_fractional_nanoseconds, tvb, PTP_AS_DT_TLV_INFORMATION_OFFSET + PTP_AS_DT_TLV_SYNCEGRESSTIMESTAMPFRACTIONALNANOSECONDS_OFFSET, 2, ENC_BIG_ENDIAN);`

Both of them are using `ptp.as.dt.syncEgressTimestamp.scaledNanoseconds` as the filter string. Using the same string will make it impossible to distinguish between them when filtering.

If you would like to display them in a combined manner, there are ways of doing that, either instead or in addition to displaying them separately. But when displayed separately, they should have different filter abbreviations.

This is the TLV: ![image](/uploads/ee2bf2db9fbc0bd9ee1c17c5ffe92e84/image.png){width=414 height=222} The syncEgressTimestamp is of type ExtendedTimestamp, defined as ![image](/uploads/0081708290e0ddefdfebe344c3117fba/image.png){width=634 height=342}. I apologize for the confusion. My intention is to split the fractionalNanoseconds into nanoseconds (UINT32) and sub-nanoseconds called fractionalNanoseconds (fractional part of the timestamp) (the remaining 16 bits). So it is one value -> should not be distinguished when filtering and should be displayed together. You suggested the option to show them together, how would I do that?

One option to show them together would be to create a FT_UINT48 field that spans the 6 bytes, declare it as `BASE_CUSTOM`, and the use a custom formatting function to handle it as a fixed point number.

Another option is to implement a FT_DOUBLE field, calculate the number from the field, and add it with `proto_tree_add_double`.

Since you only have 48 bits, it's possible to precisely store this in a IEEE 754 double without any rounding.

Here's some useful documentation:
https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/master/doc/README.dissector
Thanks for the support, I think I got it.

I realize that there are other places in the PTP dissector where a FT_UINT64 is being used for what according to the specification is clearly a EUI-64:

"The clock identity is an 8-octet array and will be presented in the form of a character array.  Network byte order is assumed...The value of the PtpClockIdentity should be taken from the IEEE EUI-64..."

https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8173

Separately, there's probably some issues with manufacturer lookups when MA-M and MA-S are used with the IEEE deprecated but commonly employed "modify a EUI-48 to an EUI-64 by shoving FF:FE bytes in there." (https://standards.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/import/documents/tutorials/eui.pdf) We need to handle that in general with EUI-64, though.
